title: Can, want, must

blocks.title: At the office in Moncton
blocks.context: Lucie invites her colleague Raj to lunch.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Raj, tu veux manger avec nous ce midi ?
lines.en: Raj, do you want to eat with us at lunch today?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: C'est gentil, mais je ne peux pas. Je dois finir mon travail avant deux heures.
lines.en: That's kind, but I can't. I have to finish my work before two o'clock.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Dommage ! Et vendredi soir ? Karim et moi, nous voulons aller au restaurant.
lines.en: Too bad! And Friday evening? Karim and I want to go to a restaurant.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Vendredi, oui, je peux ! Mais je dois rentrer tôt : je travaille samedi.
lines.en: Friday, yes, I can! But I have to go home early: I work on Saturday.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: C'est correct ! On mange à six heures ?
lines.en: That's fine! Shall we eat at six?

blocks.body: Listen for three little verbs that come before another verb: [[veux]], [[peux]], [[dois]].

blocks.title: Three verbs + an infinitive
blocks.body:
- [[pouvoir]] = can, to be able to, and also *may* (permission)
- [[vouloir]] = to want
- [[devoir]] = must, to have to

All three are irregular, and all three are usually followed by a **second verb in the infinitive**, with **no little word in between**: [[Je peux payer.]] [[Tu veux manger ?]] [[Il doit travailler.]]

Only the first verb changes with the person. The second verb never changes.

blocks.title: The present tense
head: pouvoir (can)
vouloir (want)
devoir (must)
blocks.note: The three verbs follow the same shape: [[nous]] and [[vous]] keep the stem of the infinitive (*pouv-, voul-, dev-*); the other four forms change. [[je]] and [[tu]] end in **-x** for *peux* and *veux*, but **-s** for *dois*.

blocks.title: Building the sentence
blocks.note: **Negation** goes around the first verb: [[je ne peux pas travailler]]. With a **reflexive** verb, the little pronoun still matches the subject: [[je dois me lever]], [[tu dois te lever]].

examples.fr: Nous pouvons parler anglais ou français.
examples.en: We can speak English or French.

examples.fr: Mes enfants veulent faire du ski.
examples.en: My children want to go skiing.

examples.fr: Je ne peux pas manger avec vous.
Je dois me lever à six heures.
examples.en: I have to get up at six.

blocks.title: Polite requests
blocks.body:
Three chunks cover most polite requests:

- **Asking for something:** [[Je voudrais…]] (I'd like…), softer than *je veux*: [[Je voudrais un rendez-vous, s'il vous plaît.]]
- **Asking permission:** [[Est-ce que je peux… ?]] (Can I…? / May I…?): [[Est-ce que je peux fermer la fenêtre ?]]
- **Asking someone to do something:** [[Pouvez-vous… ?]] or [[Vous pouvez… ?]]: [[Pouvez-vous parler plus lentement ?]]

Useful answers: [[Bien sûr !]] (Of course!), [[Oui, je veux bien.]] (Yes, I'd be glad to.), [[Désolé(e), je ne peux pas.]] (Sorry, I can't.)

- **No preposition:** [[Je veux manger]], not *je veux à manger*; [[je peux payer]], not *je peux de payer*.
- **Second verb in the infinitive:** [[Je dois travailler]], not *je dois travaille*.
- **Negation around the first verb:** [[Je ne veux pas danser.]]
- **“I want” to a server or a stranger sounds blunt.** Say [[Je voudrais…]] instead.
- **devoir + a noun** means *to owe*: [[Je dois vingt dollars à Karim.]] (I owe Karim twenty dollars.)

- [[peux]], [[peut]] sound the same (the vowel of [[deux]]). So do [[veux]] and [[veut]], and [[dois]] / [[doit]] (*dwa*).
- In the **ils/elles** form you hear a consonant at the end: [[peuvent]] (*v*), [[veulent]] (*l*), [[doivent]] (*v*). That is how you hear the difference between [[il peut]] and [[ils peuvent]].

[[Je voudrais]] is a special, softer form of *vouloir* (you will learn its tense, the conditional, later). For now, use it as a fixed polite chunk, like English “I would like”.

In formal writing you will also see [[Puis-je… ?]] (May I…?), a very formal way to say *Est-ce que je peux… ?* You can recognize it; you don't need to use it.

In Québec and Acadie, [[C'est correct]] does **not** mean “that's correct”. It means **it's okay, that's fine, no problem**. You'll hear it all the time:

- [[Je peux payer par carte ? — Oui, c'est correct.]]
- [[Désolé, je suis en retard ! — C'est correct.]]

In France people say [[C'est bon]] or [[Pas de problème]] in the same situations.

examples.fr: Est-ce que je peux attendre ici ? — Oui, c'est correct.
examples.en: Can I wait here? — Yes, that's fine.

blocks.prompt: Match each form to its meaning.

blocks.fr: Désolée, je ne peux pas ce soir. Je dois travailler.
blocks.en: Sorry, I can't tonight. I have to work.
blocks.prompt: Why does she say no for tonight?
blocks.explain: [[Je dois travailler]] = I have to work.

blocks.text: Je ne ___ pas manger avec vous : je ___ finir mon travail.
blocks.en: I can't eat with you: I have to finish my work.
blocks.explain: ne… pas goes around peux; dois + finir = have to finish.
vous → voulez, like the infinitive vouloir.

blocks.prompt: You are at the front desk of a clinic. Ask politely for an appointment, say one day you can't come and why, and ask the receptionist to repeat the time.
checklist: Je ne peux pas… + parce que je dois…

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Bonjour, je voudrais un rendez-vous avec le docteur, s'il vous plaît. Je ne peux pas le lundi parce que je dois travailler. Est-ce que c'est possible mardi matin ? Pardon, pouvez-vous répéter l'heure, s'il vous plaît ?
models.en: Hello, I'd like an appointment with the doctor, please. I can't on Mondays because I have to work. Is Tuesday morning possible? Sorry, can you repeat the time, please?

blocks.prompt: A friend invites you to the cinema on Saturday. Reply by text: thank them, say you can't and what you have to do, then suggest another day with tu veux… ?

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut Camille ! Merci, mais je ne peux pas samedi : je dois travailler. Tu veux aller au cinéma dimanche ? Je suis libre l'après-midi.
models.en: Hi Camille! Thanks, but I can't on Saturday: I have to work. Do you want to go to the cinema on Sunday? I'm free in the afternoon.

summary:
- Conjugate [[pouvoir, vouloir, devoir]] in the present and add an infinitive: [[je peux payer, tu veux manger, je dois travailler]]
- Make polite requests: [[Je voudrais…]] [[Est-ce que je peux… ?]] [[Pouvez-vous… ?]]
- Accept or refuse: [[Je veux bien.]] [[Désolé(e), je ne peux pas.]]

meta.notes: Dialogue: 'Je veux bien, mais je ne peux pas' -> 'C'est gentil, mais je ne peux pas' (je veux bien signals acceptance). Speaking model/checklist: 'Est-ce que mardi matin, c'est possible ?' -> 'Est-ce que c'est possible mardi matin ?'.
